source.title: Grokking Beyond Neural Networks: An Empirical Exploration with Model Complexity
source.authors: Jack William Miller; Charles O'Neill; Thang Bui

record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking in new model classes and settings, including Gaussian processes, linear regression, Bayesian neural networks, and algorithmic tasks augmented with spurious dimensions.
record.gate_note: The paper also summarizes results from other studies; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own experiments include several figure-only learning curves, for which plotted numerical values are not transcribed.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own experiments showing delayed generalization in new settings: GP classification and regression, linear regression, a BNN, and one-hidden-layer MLPs on concealed modular tasks. It varies initialization and removes regularization, so its results bear on V1, V3 and V5. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors report grokking in GP classification and regression, linear regression and BNNs, and a concealment augmentation that induces it, with a gap roughly exponential in added dimensions. They propose a model-agnostic complexity-and-error mechanism and argue grokking may occur in any model whose search is guided by complexity and error. They also say regularization appears necessary in their linear and GP cases but not in all cases.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses GP classifiers and regressors, linear regression, BNNs, and a one-hidden-layer network; it also introduces concealment by adding spurious input dimensions. These are not the original transformer modular-arithmetic training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes depend on model initialization: only GP sine-regression initialization B grokked, and the linear and GP ablations report no grokking without the complexity penalty. Grokking gaps also vary with added spurious dimensions and initialization magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: In the BNN, error falls first and complexity (KL) falls afterwards; grokking occurs where complexity decreases most. In the linear model, weights on spurious inputs are slowly driven toward zero before grokking, and GP lengthscales on spurious dimensions grow over training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A continuous complexity measure (weight norm, KL or lengthscale) declines during and around the grokking transition in non-neural and Bayesian models.

record.problems: The linear-classification grokking setup is described as specific and requires unusual initialization. The GP classification complexity measure has acknowledged comparability limitations because both the variational approximation and GP hyperparameters change during optimization. The BNN trajectory experiment has limited generality. Several reported learning curves provide plotted results without textual numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct result omitted. Detailed curve values available only in Figures 1–3, 5–6, and 14–19 are retained as figure-only or summarized only where the paper states a qualitative result.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. Only added spurious dimensions are varied.
Not tested. No circuit analysis is done, and there are no progress measures shown to anticipate the jump.
Realistic image, text or molecule data (only toy synthetic tasks are used). No explicit lazy-to-rich analysis.
The critical dataset size, ungrokking, and the claim that the generalizing solution is more efficient. Only regularization removal is tested.

missing.what: Grokking gap at zero added dimensions for each modular task: the baseline for whether the MLP groks these tasks without concealment.
BNN result that initializations giving a larger grokking gap spend longer in low-error, high-complexity regions, with grokking during the complexity decrease.
Laplace-approximation GP classification learning curves under different hyperparameter initializations.

record.verdict_notes: Removed r11–r15 from the V3 initialization label because their states cannot be determined. Concealment is a data augmentation, not an instruction to produce the behaviour, so the delays still arise from training dynamics. The linear model converging to similar weights across initializations (K.2) is trivial for a linear model and is not counted toward V6.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether reducing the training-set size increases the delay. Its concealment experiments vary added spurious dimensions instead.

The study discusses circuit-formation accounts from prior work but does not measure a generalizing circuit forming gradually, memorizing components being removed, or circuit-progress measures anticipating an accuracy jump.
It tests toy non-algorithmic tasks and initialization changes, not images, text, molecules, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The study tests removing regularization in selected settings, but not a critical dataset size, ungrokking below that size, or whether a low-norm circuit is more efficient than memorization.
The study does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax floating-point limits as causes of grokking.

rows.subject: linear regression model
rows.operation_detail: Train a linear model with SGD and a scaled weight-decay complexity term on slope classification with three added spurious dimensions and two training points.

conditions.value: Dataset 9, zero-one classification on a slope

rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over epochs
rows.value: Validation accuracy was significantly worse than training accuracy between epochs 2·10^1 and 10^3, then was very similar to training accuracy around 2·10^3; validation did not always reach 100%.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 shaded region is standard error of five training runs; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper characterizes this as grokking, but says the setup was specific and required unusual initialization. This is a toy non-algorithmic classification task.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2.1.1; Figure 1: validation trails training between approximately 20 and 1,000 epochs and becomes similar around 2,000 epochs.

relationships.condition: One-hidden-layer MLP on six concealed modular-arithmetic tasks (p=7)
relationships.reason: Validation reaches 95% well after training does. The log grokking gap correlates strongly with added dimensions (r=0.906–0.967; aggregate r=0.92) (r4–r10).
relationships.display_finding: Validation reached 95% well after training, and the logarithmic grokking gap correlated with added dimensions at r=0.906–0.967, with aggregate r=0.92.

source_check.reason: r4–r10 document delayed attainment of high validation accuracy on algorithmic tasks. Concealment correlations are correct; training-set-size dependence is untested.

relationships.condition: Toy non-algorithmic tasks: linear slope classification and GP threshold classification
relationships.reason: Delayed validation accuracy is reported on non-algorithmic synthetic data in non-neural models (r1, r2). The linear case required an unusual initialization.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy improved after a delay in linear and Gaussian-process classifiers, with the linear case requiring unusual initialization.

relationships.condition: Initialization changes in GP sine regression and the linear slope model
relationships.reason: In GP regression only initialization B groks, while A and C do not (r16–r18). In the linear model the grokking gap varies with initial weight α (r19).
relationships.display_finding: Only initialization B produced grokking in Gaussian-process regression, while A and C did not, and the linear model's delay varied with initial weight α.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Initialization changes in GP sine regression and the linear slope model
source_check.reason: r16–r19 support initialization dependence: only GP initialization B groks, and the linear model's gaps approach zero at α=1. GP kernel initialization and directional linear initialization do not establish a lazy-to-rich mechanism.

relationships.condition: MLP concealment with initialization magnitudes from 1e-8 to 1
relationships.reason: Smaller initialization only shrinks the growth in relative gap; every scale still shows grokking increasing with added dimensions (r20).
relationships.display_finding: Across initialization magnitudes from 10^-8 to 1, smaller initialization reduced relative-gap growth, but grokking still increased with added dimensions.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: MLP concealment with initialization magnitudes from 1e-8 to 1
source_check.reason: r20 shows smaller initialization moderating the growth in relative delay while concealment increases grokking across all tested magnitudes; this qualifies an initialization-based on/off account.

relationships.condition: Regularization-removal ablations in linear regression and GP classification
relationships.reason: Without weight decay or the KL complexity term, no grokking appears even after 1e6 epochs (linear) or 1e5–1e6 epochs (GP) (r21–r23). Only the low-norm-bias part of V5 is tested.
relationships.display_finding: Removing weight decay or the KL complexity term prevented grokking through 10^6 epochs in linear regression and 10^5–10^6 epochs in Gaussian-process classification.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Regularization-removal ablations in linear regression and GP classification
source_check.reason: r21–r23 explicitly report no grokking after removing the weight penalty or GP complexity term. This supports the regularization component; efficient circuits, critical dataset size and ungrokking are untested.
